findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS database data is stored unencrypted at rest. This exposes sensitive data to anyone who gains access to the underlying storage.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the RDS instance directly to the internet via a publicly routable endpoint, greatly expanding the attack surface of the database.

The database uses the well-known default administrator username 'admin' and stores the password via an unencrypted plaintext variable passed into the configuration, weakening access control on the DB.

skip_final_snapshot is true and backup_retention_period is 0, meaning no backups or final snapshots are retained, increasing data-loss and recovery risk, though this is more operational than a direct exposure.
The egress rule allows all traffic to 0.0.0.0/0, providing a data exfiltration path and a channel to command-and-control infrastructure from the database security group.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on resource '*', combining wildcard actions with a wildcard resource, which is equivalent to administrative access on those services and violates least privilege.

The database password is sourced from var.password directly into the resource and echoed into ec2 user_data as plain text; plaintext secrets in source-controlled IaC are readable by anyone with repository or describe access and must be treated as compromised.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the RDS database password (var.password) and username in plain text. User data is readable by anyone with describe-instances access, exposing production database credentials.
